rv.q: People, Places and Things is a layered and vivid piece of theatre, desperately eloquent about addiction, obliteration, pretence and performance – in theatre as in life.
Denise Gough’s electrifying portrayal will, if there is an atom of justice in this world, make her a star.
There is absolutely no doubt that Gough is the person, Wyndham's the place and this play the thing to see this spring.
For my money, Denise Gough gives the greatest stage performance since Mark Rylance in Jerusalem as Emma, an actress addicted to drink and drugs.
Gough gives a masterclass in nuance and subtlety.
It remains what it was: a glittering paean to booze and drugs delivered as a visceral, mournful howl to the skies.
This is one of those productions you simply must not let pass you by.

"Macmillan’s script is almost as prickly as its sardonic lead...The metaphors are sometimes overegged, but Gough’s raw delivery ensures Macmillan’s discourse has a visceral immediacy. She makes Emma’s articulate nihilism persuasive and simultaneously obnoxiously self-indulgent.
Her performance dignifies the West End.
This masterpiece in the making is a pivotal unexpected smash-hit few expected.

cn.t: Critics hail Macmillan's addiction drama as extraordinary, powered by Denise Gough's astounding, career-defining performance. The play's raw honesty, sharp wit, and emotional depth make it unmissable theatre that grabs audiences and doesn't let go.
